Committed by `pnpm run audit:update`. See tooling/audit-gate.mjs.

`GHSA-hp3w-g68c-fv3c` (moderate) was baselined 2026-10-06 and cannot be upgraded away:

GHSA-hp3w-g68c-fv3c (CVE pending, sprintf-js <= 1.0.3, moderate): unbounded
  precision specifiers let a caller drive unbounded formatting work. The advisory
  lists patched versions: None, and 1.0.3 is what the lock resolves, so there is
  no version to upgrade to.

- Not runtime-reachable. Traced with \pnpm why sprintf-js\: sprintf-js@1.0.3 ->
  argparse@1.0.10 -> js-yaml@3.15.2 -> @expo/cli@0.18.31 -> expo@51.0.39 ->
  @sop/mobile. That is the Expo build toolchain inside apps/mobile, which the
  repository ledger records as unbuilt. Nothing in a served request path of
  apps/web or the packages imports it, and no repository code references
  sprintf-js directly (checked by name across all tracked .mjs/.ts/.tsx/.js).

- Same category as the baselared braces advisory and the other expo-tree
  advisories already in this file: build-time tooling for a target that has not
  shipped, with no upstream fix available.

Revisit when upstream publishes a fixed sprintf-js release: remove this entry and
this note together and the gate will hold the improvement without a code change.

`GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm` (high) was baselined 2026-10-06 and cannot be upgraded away:

Restored 2026-10-06. It had been recorded on the same day and then destroyed by
  an --update run, which is why audit-gate.mjs now preserves the note instead of
  overwriting it with a fixed string.

- No patched version exists. The advisory lists patched versions: None, and the
  affected range is <= 3.0.3, which is the version already resolved here. There
  is no version to move to, so pnpm update cannot clear it.
- Not runtime-reachable. braces arrives only through build-time tooling:
  micromatch 4.0.8 -> jest-message-util, jscodeshift, metro-file-map, fast-glob.
  Nothing in a served request path imports it.
- Low practical risk. Stack exhaustion from a deeply nested glob pattern supplied
  by an attacker (CWE-674). CVSS 8.7, EPSS 0.74%.

Baselining keeps the advisory visible and tracked: counted, reported by
pnpm run audit, and the gate still fails on anything new or escalated. Remove this
entry and this note together when upstream ships a fixed braces release; the gate
will hold the improvement without a code change.

`GHSA-86w9-cpqp-85rv` (high, node-forge <= 1.4.0) is baselined and cannot be
upgraded away:

- No patched version exists. pnpm's advisory output names `>= 1.4.1`, but that
  release is not on the registry: `pnpm view node-forge@1.4.1 version` answers
  ERR_PNPM_PACKAGE_NOT_FOUND, and the registry's newest is 1.4.0 -- which is what
  the lock already resolves. An override written from the advisory text alone
  would not resolve. `npm_exists.py` in career_automation is the check that
  caught this, and it is why each of the three remaining entries was confirmed
  against the registry rather than trusted.
- Not runtime-reachable. node-forge arrives through the Expo/Sentry toolchain
  inside apps/mobile, which the ledger records as unbuilt.

Why 36 entries left this file. The seven overrides in pnpm-workspace.yaml
cleared them, in two distinct shapes. Four were deduplication: @xmldom/xmldom
(0.7.13 -> 0.9.12), postcss (8.4.49 -> 8.5.28) and send (0.18.0 -> 0.19.2) each
had a patched copy already in the lockfile beside a stale vulnerable one, so the
override only had to force the duplicate up. Their advisory floors name *lower*
versions than what was installed (postcss >=8.5.23, send >=0.19.0), so
overriding to the advisory's own number would have been a downgrade. The rest
were real major bumps: fast-xml-parser 4.5.7 -> 5.7.0, image-size 1.2.1 ->
2.0.3, tar 6.2.1 -> 7.5.21, uuid 8.3.2 -> 11.1.1.
